name: ojg-bounded-and-cancellable-parsing
instr:
Allow applications to parse untrusted JSON and SEN with caller-controlled resource budgets and context cancellation across value parsing, tokenization, and document discovery. The same policy must govern native values, gen.Node trees, permissive SEN input, readers, callbacks, channels, and pooled entry points. Calls without a budget or cancellation must retain existing behavior.

ParseLimits independently bounds consumed bytes, nesting depth, token size, and delivered documents, with zero meaning unlimited and the configured boundary remaining valid. A ParseBudget is operation-wide: chunks, token events, deliveries, scans, and rejected discovery candidates advance one account without counting input rejected beyond a boundary. Every limit failure is a LimitError matching ErrLimitExceeded, reporting its LimitKind, limit, observed usage, and preserving parser context; ordinary syntax and reader errors retain their identities. Parsers and tokenizers reject excess or cancellation before exposing the affected value, Node, token callback, channel result, or SEN function effect. Native JSON, generic JSON, SEN, and their reader forms agree on limits and usage for lexically equivalent input while preserving their existing representations, permissive rules, and reuse semantics. JSON and SEN discovery continue past ordinary malformed candidates but share scanning and candidate costs and stop delivery promptly on cancellation or exhaustion.
